server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — Adding abstract getShortcut() breaks pre-existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory providers during postInit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface adds a new abstract method getShortcut() without a default implementation. Any existing third-party implementations of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory would fail to compile or would cause runtime errors during postInit when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory iterates over all OAuth2GrantType providers and calls getShortcut() on each factory. This is a breaking change for existing providers that don't implement the new method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:102 — Removing the public Context(Context) constructor makes existing grant providers that copy contexts fail with NoSuchMethodError.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the removal of the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context class (lines 102-116 in the old code are deleted). This is a public API in server-spi-private, and any existing OAuth2GrantType implementations that relied on this copy constructor to create a copy of the context would fail at runtime with NoSuchMethodError after this change. The finding correctly identifies this as a breaking change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — A dynamically deployed grant that reuses an existing shortcut overwrites its decode mapping without collision validation, causing existing token IDs to decode as the new grant.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java lines 108-123 (getGrantTypeByShortcut method), when a new grant type is dynamically deployed, the code searches for it by shortcut and adds it to the maps. However, there's no validation that the shortcut doesn't already exist in grantsByShortcuts. If a new grant reuses an existing shortcut, line 118 `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType)` would overwrite the existing mapping, causing tokens created with the old grant type to now decode as the new grant type. The postInit method (lines 63-78) does have validation for duplicates at startup, but this runtime refresh path in getGrantTypeByShortcut lacks such validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:34 — Adding a required method to this extension SPI breaks existing external grant provider factories at load time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `getShortcut()` is added as a new abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 34). This is an SPI (Service Provider Interface) that external implementations can extend. Adding a new required method to an interface without a default implementation is a breaking change - any existing external grant provider factories that implement this interface will fail to compile/load because they don't implement the new `getShortcut()` method. The diff shows all internal implementations being updated with the new method, but external implementations would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:74 — Calling the newly abstract getShortcut method during startup makes every preexisting third-party grant factory fail with AbstractMethodError and prevents server boot.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface has a new abstract method `getShortcut()` added (line 30-34 in the interface file). In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), line 74 calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on all OAuth2GrantType provider factories. Any third-party implementation of OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that existed before this change would not have implemented this new method, causing an AbstractMethodError at runtime when the server starts and iterates through all grant type factories. This is a real backward compatibility bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483 — The access-token matcher checks the wrong two-character slice and rejects an exact grant match, so grant-type assertions silently pass for arbitrary prefixes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the isAccessTokenId matcher. Looking at the code: `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts characters at indices 3-4 (2 chars), but the token format shown in tests like 'onrtna:5678' has the grant shortcut at positions 4-5 (0-indexed: 'on'=session, 'rt'=token, 'na'=grant). So substring(4,6) would be correct. Additionally, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when it MATCHES, which is inverted logic - it should return false when it does NOT match. This is a real bug that would cause the matcher to incorrectly pass/fail.
